extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and practitioners handling inter partes reexamination
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural standards governing inter partes reexamination before the USPTO, including appeals to the Federal Circuit, duty of disclosure, interview prohibitions, notification of related proceedings, and merger/suspension of copending reexaminations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of appeal to the Federal Circuit
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner, or a third-party requester in an inter partes reexamination proceeding who is a party to an appeal to the Board and who is dissatisfied with the decision of the Board may appeal only to the United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit (35 U.S.C. 141; 37 CFR 1.983).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal to the Federal Circuit is subject to exhausting rehearing rights per 37 CFR 41.81; for proceedings commenced on or after Nov. 2, 2002 third-party requesters have the right to appeal and be parties to appeals (35 U.S.C. 315 revisions). For proceedings commenced prior to Nov. 2, 2002 third-party requesters are precluded from appealing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural steps required to perfect an appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellant must: (1) timely file a written notice of appeal in the USPTO directed to the Director in accordance with §§ 1.302 and 1.304; (2) in the Federal Circuit, file a copy of the notice of appeal and pay the fee per the Federal Circuit rules; and (3) serve a copy of the notice of appeal on every other party in the reexamination proceeding as provided in § 1.248 (37 CFR 1.983(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation in another party's appeal requires, within 14 days of service of the notice, filing a written notice electing to participate in the Office, filing a copy in the Federal Circuit, and serving a copy on all other parties (37 CFR 1.983(e)). Cross-appeals follow 37 CFR 1.983(c)-(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on civil action under 35 U.S.C. 145
rubrics_metrics.description: The remedy by civil action under 35 U.S.C. 145 (action in U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia) is not available to patent owners or third-party requesters in inter partes reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties dissatisfied with a Board decision in inter partes reexamination are limited to appeal to the Federal Circuit; 35 U.S.C. 145 was amended and does not provide an avenue for inter partes reexamination review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of disclosure in inter partes reexamination (37 CFR 1.933)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual associated with the patent owner in an inter partes reexamination proceeding has a duty of candor and good faith to disclose to the Office all information known to that individual to be material to patentability in the reexamination proceeding as set forth in § 1.555(a) and (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The duty is deemed satisfied by filing a paper compliant with § 1.555(a) and (b). Responsibility rests on the designated individuals; the Office will not evaluate compliance in the reexamination proceeding. Questions of compliance raised during the proceeding will be noted as unresolved under § 1.906(c). Fraud or intentional misconduct constitutes noncompliance with § 1.555(a). See MPEP § 2280 for further discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on interviews about merits (37 CFR 1.955)
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be no interviews in an inter partes reexamination proceeding which discuss the merits of the proceeding; any communications directed to the merits must be in writing and filed with the Office for entry into the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural matters accessible from the public file may be discussed. Telephone calls limited to completing or correcting the record (non-merits matters) may be made at the Office's discretion but must NOT be made by the examiner or any Office employee who addresses the proceeding on its merits; such calls should be made by paralegal or support staff. Any subsequent Office communication must state that the telephone call was limited solely to the non-merits matter. Informal amendments that would be tantamount to an ex parte interview will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of prior or concurrent proceedings (37 CFR 1.985)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner shall call the Office's attention to any prior or concurrent proceedings in which the patent is or was involved (including interference, reissue, reexamination, or litigation) and the results of such proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any person may file a paper notifying the Office of such prior or concurrent proceedings, but the paper must be limited to mere notice without discussion of issues of the current inter partes reexamination; submissions not so limited will be returned. The Office may accept copies of notices and decisions for entry to ensure a complete file, but will not enter party arguments (e.g., memoranda). Non-merit procedural decisions generally will not be entered. If submissions are voluminous the Office may return/expunge/discard them; submitters should limit to relevant notice. Highlighting or markup goes beyond bare notice and is improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merger or suspension of multiple copending reexamination proceedings (37 CFR 1.989)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reexamination is ordered while a prior inter partes reexamination is pending, the Office may merge the two proceedings or suspend one of them; where merger is ordered, the merged examination normally results in issuance and publication of a single reexamination certificate under § 1.997.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether merger or suspension is appropriate is within Office discretion (OPLA). Suspension is only for exceptional circumstances (requires express written OPLA approval) and will not be granted when there is an outstanding Office action. The statutory mandate of conducting inter partes reexaminations with 'special dispatch' (35 U.S.C. 314(c)) counsels against merger when it would unduly delay a first proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file subsequent reexamination requests when one is pending
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing eligibility for a second/subsequent request depends on the type of the earlier pending reexamination: if earlier is inter partes, a subsequent inter partes request cannot be filed by the same third-party requester or its privy; if earlier is ex parte, any party other than the patent owner can file an inter partes request; ex parte subsequent requests may be filed by any party including the patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See explicit case breakdowns: Case(1)(a)/(b) and Case(2)(a)/(b) in MPEP § 2686.01. The second/subsequent request must raise a substantial new question of patentability based on the art cited (see MPEP § 2640) for the request to be granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of merger decision and effect on prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: No decision on merging should be made until reexamination has been ordered for both proceedings and there is no longer an opportunity for filing a patent owner's statement and/or requester’s reply; if merged, prosecution will be conducted at the most advanced point possible for the first proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the first proceeding is at ACP (Action Closing Prosecution) stage, prosecution will ordinarily be reopened to consider any new substantial question from the second request unless no new rejection/change of position is warranted. Patent owner will be given opportunity to respond to new rejections in a merged proceeding prior to issuance of ACP. The Office will normally assign Request 2 to the same examiner as Request 1 and consult the Reexamination Legal Advisor (RLA) when deciding Request 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for merged proceedings (identical claims and filings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where merger is ordered, the decision should include a requirement that the patent owner maintain identical claims in both files and require that responses/comments be a single response/comment paper addressed to both files, filed in duplicate and signed for entry in both files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims are not identical at the time of merger, the patent owner is given one month to provide an amendment to make the claims the same in each file (a 'housekeeping' amendment). The housekeeping amendment must not address any issue of patentability. Failure to timely submit identical amendments may result in rejection of any non-identical claim under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as indefinite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and processing of examiner actions in merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In merged proceedings a single combined examiner's action will be prepared, containing control numbers of both proceedings on every page; clerical and CRU processing rules apply to produce copies and to provide actions to requesters and the patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When NIRC(s) (Notices of Intent To Issue Inter Partes Reexamination Certificate) are appropriate, plural notices will be printed and both reexamination files processed. CRU prepares the file as specified in MPEP § 2687 before release to Office of Data Management. When merged, the examiner should prepare actions at the most advanced point possible for the first proceeding and consult the RLA as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing limits on submissions of copending proceedings and litigation materials
rubrics_metrics.description: While inter partes reexamination is pending, third party submissions filed after the order date ordinarily are not entered unless by the third party requester; the Office will accept for the reexamination file copies of notices of suits and decisions from litigations or other proceedings but will not enter papers that make arguments in the other proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters should provide notice identifying application/proceeding numbers and status rather than submitting full copending reexamination proceedings/applications (which might be mistaken for new requests). The Office may return/expunge/discard submissions considered not permitted or excessively voluminous; submitters should limit to bare notice and relevant decisions.
